# Regulation (EU) 2024/3005 (ESGR): verified article map

Verified against the official text in `library/text/L1-ESGR.txt` (OJ L, 12.12.2024, 48 pages) on 23 Oct 2026. Quotes are exact. For any answer, re-quote from the library text rather than from this summary.

**Dates.** Published in the OJ on 12 Dec 2024. In force "on the twentieth day following that of its publication", i.e. 1 Jan 2025 (some ESMA documents say 3 Jan). Applies "from 2 July 2026" (Art 53).

## Title I: Scope and definitions
| Art | What it says (key words quoted) |
|---|---|
| 1 | Subject matter: integrity, transparency, responsibility, good governance and independence of ESG rating activities. |
| 2(1) | Applies to ratings by providers "operating in the Union". **EU-established**: (i) "issue and publish their ESG ratings on their website or through other means", or (ii) distribute them "by subscription or other contractual relationships" to EU regulated financial undertakings, undertakings under the Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU or the Transparency Directive 2004/109/EC, or EU institutions and Member State public authorities. **Non-EU**: only case (ii). |
| 2(2) | Exclusions (a)-(q): (a) private ratings not for disclosure; (b) internal or in-house/intragroup use by regulated financial undertakings (Q&A 2806); (c) ratings issued by regulated financial undertakings and embedded in products regulated by listed EU law and disclosed to third parties. If disclosed in marketing, the undertaking must put the Annex III point 1 information on its website and link to it, and national competent authorities monitor this; (d) non-EU ratings obtained at the user's "own exclusive initiative" with "no substitute" (reverse solicitation, narrowly drawn); (e) ESG data; (f) credit ratings and their ESG inputs; (g) products incorporating an element of a rating, incl. investment research; (h) EuGB external reviews; (i) external reviews and SPOs "to the extent that [they] do not contain ESG ratings" (Q&A 2807); (j) public-authority ratings not commercial; (k) "ESG ratings issued by an authorised ESG rating provider where such ratings are published or distributed by a third party"; (l) ESCB; (m) SFDR Art 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13 disclosures; (n) Taxonomy Art 5, 6, 8 disclosures; (o) accreditation/certification-only ratings; (p) labels not disclosing a rating; (q) non-profit, non-commercial ratings, **but** non-profits charging rated items or users are in scope. |
| 2(3) | Joint ESAs RTS on the content of the 2(2)(c) marketing disclosures. **Not adopted or found as of Oct 2026.** |
| 3(1) | "'ESG rating' means an opinion or a score, or a combination of both, … that is based on both an established methodology and a defined ranking system of rating categories, irrespective of whether such ESG rating is labelled as 'ESG rating', 'ESG opinion' or 'ESG score'". Q&A 2853: a ranking system is an "ordinal or hierarchical structure" with "two or more pre-determined rating categories, including the minimum and maximum levels". |
| 3(2)-(4) | ESG opinion (analyst directly involved); ESG score ("based only on a pre-established statistical or algorithmic system or model"); ESG rating provider ("legal person … on a professional basis"). |

## Title II: Getting permission to operate
| Art | What it says |
|---|---|
| 4 | Any provider must be subject to one route: ESMA authorisation (Art 6), equivalence (10), endorsement (11) or recognition (12); small providers use Art 5. |
| 5 | **Small EU providers** (Accounting Directive Art 3(2)/3(5) first subparagraph, i.e. small undertaking or small group). They are subject **only** to "Article 15(1), (5) and (7), Articles 23 and 24 and Articles 32 to 37", after notifying and being registered. ESMA decides "within 90 working days". After 3 years, or on ceasing to be small, all rules apply and they must apply for authorisation "within six months". They may opt in early (5(4)). Q&As 2737-2740. |
| 6 | Application to ESMA with Annex I information (RTS 2026/1119), in any official EU language. 6(4) comply "at all times"; **6(5) notify "any material changes … including any opening or closing of a branch … without undue delay"** (Q&A 2856). |
| 7 | ESMA checks completeness **within 25 working days**, then decides **within 90 working days** of the completeness notice, extendable to **120** (endorsement, outsourcing or Art 22 exemption). No decision in time means the application is "deemed rejected". |
| 8 | Fully reasoned decision; authorisation "effective for the entire territory of the Union". |
| 9 | Suspension or withdrawal: renounced or no ratings for 12 months; false statements; conditions no longer met; "seriously or repeatedly infringed". |
| 10 | **Equivalence** (non-EU): home authorisation and supervision + notification to ESMA + Commission equivalence decision + cooperation arrangements. ESMA completeness check 20 working days, outcome within 60. **No equivalence decision as of Oct 2026.** |
| 11 | **Endorsement**: an EU-authorised provider endorses ratings of a **same-group** non-EU provider. Conditions include minimum substance (premises, bank account, analytical and decision-making presence), "requirements which are at least as stringent as the requirements of this Regulation", monitoring expertise, an objective reason, and ESMA information access. Decision "within 45 working days" of a complete application, at most 85. The endorser "shall remain fully responsible". ESMA may require it to cease (11(6)). |
| 12 | **Recognition**: only for non-EU providers whose annual net turnover is **below the small-undertaking ceiling** (Accounting Directive Art 3(2), second subparagraph; Art 3(5) for groups) "for each of the last three consecutive years", and only until an equivalence decision exists. Requires a legal representative in the EU, Annex I information, and a list of ratings for EU distribution; decision within 90 working days. When no longer meeting the conditions: notify ESMA within 3 months and apply for authorisation within 12. **Large non-EU groups therefore need endorsement via an EU entity, an EU-authorised entity, or a future equivalence decision.** |
| 13 | Cooperation arrangements with third-country authorities. |
| 14 | Public register of authorised, Art 5-registered, equivalent, endorsing/endorsed and recognised providers. **From 1 Jan 2028** the Art 19(1) and Art 23(1) information also goes to ESAP in data-extractable format. |

## Title III, Chapter 1: Organisation (Arts 15-22)
| Art | Requirement (exact key words) |
|---|---|
| 15(1)-(6) | Independence "including from all political and economic influences or constraints"; rules and procedures; adequate systems; written policies on thorough analysis; due diligence so business interests do not impair independence; sound administrative and accounting procedures and internal controls. |
| 15(7) | "rating methodologies … that are rigorous, systematic, independent and capable of justification and shall apply those rating methodologies continuously and in a transparent manner." |
| 15(8) | "review the rating methodologies … on an ongoing basis and at least annually." |
| 15(9) | Evaluate systems, resources and procedures "at least annually". |
| 15(10) | "a permanent, independent and effective oversight function". |
| 15(11) | Information of sufficient quality from reliable sources; state the rating is the provider's own opinion. |
| 15(12) | Notify the rated item "during its working hours and at least two full working days before the first issuance of the ESG rating". On request, provide the specified Annex III information, the date of the last data update, etc. (Q&As 2716, 2717, 2719, 2890, 2891). |
| 15(13)-(14) | No trade-secret disclosure; rating changes only per the methodologies published under Art 23. |
| 16 | "ESG rating providers shall not provide any of the following activities: (a) consulting activities to investors or undertakings"; (b) credit ratings; (c) benchmarks; (d) investment services and activities; (e) statutory audit or sustainability assurance; (f) credit institution, insurance or reinsurance activities. (d) and (f) are allowed with safeguards; (c) only with ESMA authorisation of measures (30 working days); assessment staff barred from (a), (b), (e). RTS 2026/872. Q&A 2889. |
| 17 | Staff competence; no fee negotiation; trading bans; recusal for 1-year relationships; confidentiality; no gifts; whistleblowing; 1-year look-back; 9-month cooling-off. |
| 18 | "keep the information … for at least five years and in such a form that it is possible to replicate and fully understand" each rating (Annex I and II records). |
| 19 | Published complaints procedure (grounds: data or factual errors, methodology application, representativeness). |
| 20 | Reasoned concerns; non-small providers "shall endeavour to reply to the reasoned concerns within 30 working days of receipt". |
| 21 | Outsourcing must not impair internal control or ESMA supervision (Annex II point 2 conditions). |
| 22 | Small providers may seek exemption from Art 15(6), (8), (10). |

## Chapter 2: Transparency (Arts 23-24) and Chapter 3: Conflicts (Arts 25-27)
| Art | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 23 | Publish methodologies, models and key assumptions (Annex I(d), Annex III point 1) in a separate website section, at the latest when issuing starts. "Separate E, S and G ratings shall be provided rather than a single ESG rating that aggregates E, S and G factors"; an aggregate is allowed with the Annex III 1(h) weighting disclosure. RTS 2026/871. |
| 24 | Annex III point 2 information to users, rated items and issuers on an ongoing basis. When authorising a user to disclose a rating, attach a link to the Annex III point 1 information. |
| 25 | Governance; conflict prevention; ESMA can require mitigation or cessation (25(3)); cross-holding limits; disclose conflicts to ESMA; "review their operations to identify potential conflicts of interest at least annually". |
| 26 | Staff conflicts, remuneration, information barriers; management approval before distribution (26(2)). |
| 27 | Fees "fair, reasonable, transparent and non-discriminatory"; pricing evidence on request. |

## Chapter 4: Supervision by ESMA (Arts 28-42)
| Art | What it says |
|---|---|
| 28 | "ESMA, the Commission or any Member State public authorities shall not interfere with the content of ESG ratings or methodologies." |
| 29 | ESMA guidelines on cooperation and on endorsement (endorsement guidelines due 2 Oct 2025; still at consultation stage); **annual report** on application, measures and fines; **annual list with market shares** (by EU turnover at group level). |
| 30 | Each Member State designates a competent authority by 2 Apr 2026. |
| 31 | Powers do not reach legally privileged material. |
| 32-34 | Requests for information, general investigations, on-site inspections. |
| 35 | Measures: suspend or withdraw; "temporarily prohibit … publishing or distributing ESG ratings"; order an end to the infringement; fines; public notices. Can also be used against providers operating **without** permission or misusing an Art 2(2) exclusion (35(2)), and ESMA may investigate third parties that enable them. Criteria in 35(5). Decisions published within 10 working days; ESMA may require the provider to inform its users (35(7)). |
| 36 | Fine maximum "10 % of the total annual net turnover"; for group members, **consolidated turnover of the ultimate parent** (36(2)); at least the benefit gained (36(4)). |
| 37 | Periodic penalty payment "shall be 3 % of the average daily turnover" (2% of daily income for natural persons), daily, for "a maximum period of six months". |
| 38 | Fines published unless seriously jeopardising markets or disproportionate; administrative and enforceable; paid to the EU budget. |
| 39-41 | Procedure (RTS 2026/904); right to be heard; CJEU "unlimited jurisdiction" to annul, reduce or increase fines. |
| 42 | Fees proportionate to turnover (Delegated Reg 2026/910). |
| 43-46 | Delegation to national authorities, information exchange, professional secrecy. |

## Titles IV-V
| Art | What it says |
|---|---|
| 47-48 | Delegated acts; committee procedure. |
| 49 | Adds **SFDR Art 13(3)**: a financial market participant or adviser that **issues** and discloses an ESG rating in marketing must publish the Annex III point 1 information and link to it (joint ESAs RTS to follow). |
| 50 | Adds ESGR to the ESAP Regulation 2023/2859 annex. |
| 51 | Existing providers "notify ESMA by 2 August 2026" and "apply … within four months of 2 July 2026" (i.e. 2 Nov 2026), or "cease their activities". Once notified they are temporarily listed and may continue (and endorse) until decided. Small existing providers notify "no later than 2 November 2026". |
| 52 | Commission evaluation "by 2 January 2029", including whether **ESG data products** should be brought into scope and whether the Art 28 non-interference principle worked. |
| 53 | Entry into force and application (above). |

## Annexes
- **Annex I**, application content: (a)-(n), incl. ownership, senior management, staff numbers, market coverage, methodologies (use of SFDR/CSRD data, science, Paris targets), conflicts policies, outsourcing, other activities incl. endorsement, Art 16(2)/(3) measures, prior activities.
- **Annex II**, records and outsourcing: per-rating analyst and approver identities, solicited or unsolicited, action date; methodology developers and approvers; fee and user accounts; procedures and methodologies; work papers and non-public information; compliance procedures; **"changes in, or deviations from, standard procedures and methodologies"**; complaints. Outsourcing conditions (a)-(f).
- **Annex III point 1**, public disclosures (a)-(q): methodology overview and changes (backward or forward-looking, time horizon); industry classification; **data sources, processes, estimation and update frequency**; ownership; scientific basis; objective and materiality (risk vs impact, double-materiality proportions); scope (E, S, G or aggregate); (h) **E/S/G weights and method**; topics vs ESRS; absolute vs relative; **(k) use of AI, with its limitations and risks**; fee criteria and business model; limitations; conflict risks; Paris and international agreements; information limits.
- **Annex III point 2**, to users and rated items: granular methodology (KPIs and weights per E/S/G; per-category results for aggregates; **shortcomings and fixes; revision policy; reasons when a rating moved because of material methodology, model, assumption or data changes**; last revision date; taxonomy-alignment correlation); granular data (source types, assurance, CSRD/ESRS use, transition plans; estimation and industry averages; **data update and historical revision policies, last update date; "data quality controls, their frequency and the remediation process"**; steps on data limits); engagement and site visits; unsolicited-rating statement; AI methodology explanation; how major new information was handled.
